name: Kuo 2016 IC/BPS
question: Does suburothelial onabotulinumtoxinA added to hydrodistension reduce pain more than saline injection and hydrodistension in refractory IC/BPS?

design.population: Sixty patients with IC/BPS refractory to conventional treatment, including eight men and 52 women, had a mean age of 50.8 ± 13.9 years.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods and Results

verdictNote: Pain reduction favored onabotulinumtoxinA at week 8; follow-up was short.
takeaway: In refractory IC/BPS, suburothelial onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U plus hydrodistension reduced pain more at week 8 than saline injection plus hydrodistension (mean VAS change −2.6 versus −0.9; P = 0.021).

reports.label: Primary randomized report
reports.citation: Kuo HC, Jiang YH, Tsai YC, et al. "Intravesical botulinum toxin-A injections reduce bladder pain of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome refractory to conventional treatment - A prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2016;35(5):609-614. doi:10.1002/nau.22760

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to week 8; mean difference is onabotulinumtoxinA minus saline
results.note: Mean difference calculated from the two reported means; the abstract calls the between-group reduction significant.

results.measure: Overall success; definition and assessment time not supplied in abstract
results.note: 26/40 is 65%, although the abstract prints 63%; 3/20 is 15%.
The abstract reports a significant between-group difference without values.

harms.label: Adverse events
harms.note: The abstract reports no between-group difference without event types or rates.

values.ctl: equivalent amount of normal saline plus hydrodistension
